# Overview

This document runs a reusable hierarchical clustering pipeline on pre-normalised
single-cell data. The main steps are:

1. **AWST normalisation** and gene filtering via `gene_filter()` (`poscount = TRUE` for single-cell data, `FALSE` for bulk samples: parameter `single_cell`)
2. **Hierarchical clustering** with Euclidean distance and Ward's linkage; the distance matrix, the data matrix selected by the AWST gene filtering and the annotation data frame (if present) are saved in a separate distance file (`_AWST_dist.RData`)
3. **Calinski-Harabasz index** to guide the choice of the optimal number of clusters
4. **Visualisation** with annotated dendrogram, colour bars (clusterings first, from the largest number of clusters, then the annotation variables) and legends in the top-right corner (clusterings and annotation variables)
5. **Silhouette plots of the clusterings** (Figure 3), generated from the distance file (matrix `ddist`) and coloured as the clusters of the dendrogram
6. **Joint analysis of the clusterings and the annotation variables** listed in the `annot_vars` parameter, starting from the joint (two-way) distributions with their marginals, followed by the chi-squared test of independence and the ECA and ECP indices

All key parameters are exposed in the YAML `params` block and can be changed
without touching the code, or passed programmatically via `rmarkdown::render()`.

## 1.1b Helper — `as_param_vector()`

`params$cluster_sizes` may arrive as a string (`"3, 5, 7"`), a list, or an atomic
vector depending on how YAML serialises it. This helper always normalises the value
into a standard R vector.

```{r fn-as-integer-vector}
#' Coerce cluster_sizes / palettes to an R vector regardless of how
#' YAML passed the value (string, list, or atomic vector).
#'
#' @param x   Raw value from params (e.g. string "3,5,7", list, or vector)
#' @param FUN Coercion function: as.integer (default) or as.character
#' @return Atomic vector of the requested type
as_param_vector <- function(x, FUN = as.integer) {
  if (is.character(x) && length(x) == 1) {
    # e.g. "3, 5, 7" or "c(3, 5, 7)"
    x <- gsub("[c()\\s]", "", x)          # strip c( ) and spaces
    x <- strsplit(x, "[,;]+")[[1]]          # split on comma or semicolon
    x <- x[nzchar(trimws(x))]              # drop empty tokens
  }
  if (is.list(x)) x <- unlist(x)
  FUN(x)
}

#' Coerce a parameter holding NAMES (annotation variables, palettes) to a character
#' vector. Unlike as_param_vector() it never alters the characters of the names.
#'
#' @param x NULL, a character vector, a list, or one string such as "patient, Sex"
#'          or "c('patient', 'Sex')"
#' @return  Character vector (character(0) if x is NULL or empty)
as_name_vector <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(character(0))
  if (is.list(x)) x <- unlist(x)
  x <- as.character(x)
  if (length(x) == 1) {
    x <- gsub("^\\s*c\\(|\\)\\s*$|[\"']", "", x)   # "c('a', 'b')" -> "a, b"
    x <- strsplit(x, "[,;]+")[[1]]
  }
  x <- trimws(x)
  x[nzchar(x)]
}

#' Word used for the observations: "cells" (single-cell data) or "samples" (bulk)
#'
#' @param single_cell TRUE for single-cell data, FALSE for bulk samples
#' @param plural      TRUE = "cells" / "samples", FALSE = "cell" / "sample"
#' @return            Character string
obs_label <- function(single_cell = TRUE, plural = TRUE) {
  word <- if (isTRUE(single_cell)) "cell" else "sample"
  if (plural) paste0(word, "s") else word
}

#' Regex matching any of the accepted RData extensions (.RData, .rdata, .rda),
#' case-insensitively.
.RDATA_EXT_REGEX <- "\\.(RData|rdata|rda)$"

#' Derive a new file path by replacing the RData extension (.RData/.rdata/.rda,
#' case-insensitive) of `file` with `suffix`.
#'
#' @param file   Original file path, ending in .RData, .rdata, or .rda
#' @param suffix Replacement string (e.g. "_clustering.RData")
#' @return       Derived path
derive_rdata_path <- function(file, suffix) {
  sub(.RDATA_EXT_REGEX, suffix, file, ignore.case = TRUE)
}

#' Resolve a data file on disk by trying each of the accepted RData
#' extensions (.RData, .rdata, .rda) appended to `base`.
#'
#' @param base Path without extension (e.g. "MyDataset_annotation")
#' @return     First existing path among base+ext, or base+".RData" if none exist
resolve_rdata_file <- function(base) {
  candidates <- paste0(base, c(".RData", ".rdata", ".rda"))
  found <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)]
  if (length(found) > 0) found[1] else candidates[1]
}

#' Return the unique values of `x` that are not valid R colours (NA is ignored).
#' Used to protect rect()/legend() from invalid colour names.
#'
#' @param x Vector of colour names / hex codes
#' @return  Character vector of the invalid values (character(0) if all valid)
.invalid_colors <- function(x) {
  u <- unique(as.character(x))
  u <- u[!is.na(u)]
  u[!vapply(u, function(z) tryCatch({ grDevices::col2rgb(z); TRUE },
                                    error = function(e) FALSE), logical(1))]
}

#' Kelly's 20 chromatic "colours of maximum contrast" (white and black left out),
#' in the order that keeps the first n colours as different from each other as possible.
.CONTRAST_COLORS <- c("#F3C300", "#875692", "#F38400", "#A1CAF1", "#BE0032",
                      "#C2B280", "#848482", "#008856", "#E68FAC", "#0067A5",
                      "#F99379", "#604E97", "#F6A600", "#B3446C", "#DCD300",
                      "#882D17", "#8DB600", "#654522", "#E25822", "#2B3D26")

#' Candidate colours of a palette, in order of preference.
#'
#' @param palette_name "contrast" (high-contrast palette, the default) or the name
#'                     of an RColorBrewer palette
#' @param n            Number of colours needed
#' @return             Character vector of unique colours; when no colour has been
#'                     used yet, the colours to use are the first `n`
.palette_pool <- function(palette_name, n) {
  if (tolower(palette_name) %in% c("contrast", "kelly"))
    return(.CONTRAST_COLORS)
  if (!palette_name %in% rownames(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info))
    stop("Unknown palette: '", palette_name,
         "' (use \"contrast\" or an RColorBrewer palette name).")
  maxc <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal.info[palette_name, "maxcolors"]
  full <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(maxc, palette_name)
  own  <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(max(3, min(n, maxc)), palette_name)
  unique(c(own[seq_len(min(n, length(own)))], full))
}
```

## 1.2 `prepare_clustering()`

Applies AWST normalisation, filters genes, and computes the hierarchical clustering.

```{r fn-prepare}
#' @param input_file     Path to RData file containing matrix `ddata`
#' @param output_file    Where to save the output RData (NULL = auto-derived)
#' @param hclust_method  Linkage method for hclust (default: "ward.D2")
#' @param poscount       poscount argument passed to awst() (TRUE for single-cell data)
#' @param full_quantile  full_quantile argument passed to awst()
#' @param force          If TRUE, recompute even if output already exists (default: FALSE)
#' @param dist_file      Where to save the distance file (NULL = input name +
#'                       "_AWST_dist.RData"). It contains the distance matrix `ddist`, the
#'                       data matrix `exprData` selected by the AWST gene filtering and the
#'                       annotation data frame `annotation.df`, if present
#' @param annotation_file RData file with the object `annotation.df`, used when the input
#'                       file does not contain it (NULL = no annotation file)
#' @return Invisible list: hhc, nrow_exprData, ncol_exprData, aCalinski, output_file,
#'         dist_file
prepare_clustering <- function(
    input_file,
    output_file    = NULL,
    hclust_method  = "ward.D2",
    poscount       = TRUE,
    full_quantile  = TRUE,
    force          = TRUE,
    dist_file      = NULL,
    annotation_file = NULL
) {
  if (is.null(output_file))
    output_file <- derive_rdata_path(input_file, "_AWST_hclust.RData")
  if (is.null(dist_file))
    dist_file   <- derive_rdata_path(input_file, "_AWST_dist.RData")

  # -- skip se entrambi gli output esistono già e force = FALSE --
  if (file.exists(output_file) && !file.exists(dist_file) && !force)
    message("Distance file not found (", dist_file, "): recomputing.")
  if (file.exists(output_file) && file.exists(dist_file) && !force) {
    message("⏭  Outputs already exist, loading from: ", output_file)
    env <- new.env()
    tryCatch(
      load(output_file, envir = env),
      error = function(e) stop(
        "Impossibile leggere l'output esistente '", output_file, "'.\n",
        "  Causa: ", conditionMessage(e), "\n",
        "  Prova a richiamare con force = TRUE per rigenerarlo."
      )
    )
    return(invisible(list(
      hhc           = env$hhc,
      nrow_exprData = env$nrow_exprData,
      ncol_exprData = env$ncol_exprData,
      aCalinski     = env$aCalinski,
      output_file   = output_file,
      dist_file     = dist_file
    )))
  }

  # -- verifica che il file di input esista prima di aprirlo --
  if (!file.exists(input_file))
    stop(
      "File di input non trovato: '", input_file, "'.\n",
      "  Directory corrente: ", getwd()
    )

  env <- new.env()
  tryCatch(
    load(input_file, envir = env),
    error = function(e) stop(
      "Impossibile leggere '", input_file, "'.\n",
      "  Causa: ", conditionMessage(e)
    )
  )
  if (!exists("ddata", envir = env))
    stop("'", input_file, "' does not contain an object named 'ddata'.")
  ddata <- env$ddata

  # -- annotation data frame, if present (in the input file or in annotation_file) --
  annotation.df <- NULL
  if (exists("annotation.df", envir = env, inherits = FALSE)) {
    annotation.df <- env$annotation.df
  } else if (!is.null(annotation_file) && file.exists(annotation_file)) {
    env_annot <- new.env()
    load(annotation_file, envir = env_annot)
    if (exists("annotation.df", envir = env_annot, inherits = FALSE))
      annotation.df <- env_annot$annotation.df
  }
  message("→ annotation.df: ", if (is.null(annotation.df)) "not found" else "found")

  message("→ AWST...")
  exprData <- awst(ddata, poscount = poscount, full_quantile = full_quantile)
  exprData <- gene_filter(exprData)
  message(sprintf("  Dimensions: %d genes x %d cells", nrow(exprData), ncol(exprData)))

  exprData      <- t(exprData)
  nrow_exprData <- nrow(exprData)   # cellule
  ncol_exprData <- ncol(exprData)   # geni

  message("→ Distance matrix + hclust (", hclust_method, ")...")
  ddist <- dist(exprData)
  hhc   <- hclust(ddist, method = hclust_method)

  message("→ Calinski index...")
  aCalinski <- calinski(hhc)

  save(hhc, nrow_exprData, ncol_exprData, aCalinski, file = output_file)
  message("✔  Saved: ", output_file)

  # distance file: distance matrix, selected data matrix and annotation (if present)
  dist_objects <- c("ddist", "exprData", if (!is.null(annotation.df)) "annotation.df")
  save(list = dist_objects, file = dist_file)
  message("✔  Saved: ", dist_file, " (", paste(dist_objects, collapse = ", "), ")")

  invisible(list(
    hhc           = hhc,
    nrow_exprData = nrow_exprData,
    ncol_exprData = ncol_exprData,
    aCalinski     = aCalinski,
    output_file   = output_file,
    dist_file     = dist_file
  ))
}
```

## 1.3 `add_clustering_cut()`

Cuts the tree at *k* clusters and assigns labels and colours.

When several cuts are drawn, a group made of **exactly the same cells** as a group of a
cut already coloured keeps the **same colour**. Only the remaining groups receive new
colours, taken from the palette of the cut (by default the high-contrast one) and
never reused for a different group.

```{r fn-cut}
#' @param hhc               hclust object
#' @param clustering.df     Data frame with a 'barcode' column (and the columns of the
#'                          cuts already added, used to find coinciding groups)
#' @param clust.colorCode   Named colour vector already assigned
#' @param no_of_clusters    k for cutree()
#' @param palette_name      RColorBrewer palette name
#' @param colors            Optional colours for this cut; if given (at least k), they
#'                          are used as they are, without inheriting colours
#' @param clustering.prefix Column name prefix (default: "clust")
#' @param short.prefix      Short prefix for cluster labels (default: "c")
#' @return List: updated clustering.df, clust.colorCode, cut height hh
#'         (the cut line is drawn later by .draw_clustering_figure())
add_clustering_cut <- function(
    hhc,
    clustering.df,
    clust.colorCode,
    no_of_clusters,
    palette_name,
    colors            = NULL,
    clustering.prefix = "clust",
    short.prefix      = "c"
) {
  clustering_name     <- paste0(clustering.prefix, no_of_clusters)
  clustering_name.col <- paste0(clustering_name, ".col")

  hh <- (
    hhc$height[length(hhc$height) - no_of_clusters + 2] +
    hhc$height[length(hhc$height) - no_of_clusters + 1]
  ) / 2

  # -- group labels (c<k>1, c<k>2, ...) --
  labels_pool <- c(paste(1:9), letters)
  lab_levels  <- paste0(short.prefix, no_of_clusters, labels_pool)[seq_len(no_of_clusters)]
  grp         <- as.integer(cutree(hhc, k = no_of_clusters))
  grp_lab     <- factor(grp, levels = seq_len(no_of_clusters), labels = lab_levels)

  # -- one colour per group --
  col_of_group <- stats::setNames(rep(NA_character_, no_of_clusters), lab_levels)

  if (!is.null(colors) && length(colors) >= no_of_clusters) {
    # colours explicitly requested by the user: used as they are
    col_of_group[] <- colors[seq_len(no_of_clusters)]
  } else {
    # (1) a group with exactly the same cells as a group of a previous cut
    #     inherits the colour of that group
    prev_cols <- grep(paste0("^", clustering.prefix, "[0-9]+\\.col$"),
                      colnames(clustering.df), value = TRUE)
    prev_cols <- setdiff(prev_cols, clustering_name.col)
    for (pc in prev_cols) {
      prev_lab <- as.character(clustering.df[[sub("\\.col$", "", pc)]])
      prev_col <- as.character(clustering.df[[pc]])
      for (j in seq_len(no_of_clusters)) {
        if (!is.na(col_of_group[j])) next
        in_j <- grp == j
        lv   <- unique(prev_lab[in_j])
        if (length(lv) == 1 && sum(prev_lab == lv) == sum(in_j))
          col_of_group[j] <- prev_col[which(in_j)[1]]
      }
    }

    # (2) remaining groups: new colours from the palette, not used so far
    todo <- which(is.na(col_of_group))
    if (length(todo) > 0) {
      used <- toupper(c(unname(clust.colorCode), col_of_group[!is.na(col_of_group)]))
      pool <- .palette_pool(palette_name, no_of_clusters)
      pool <- pool[!toupper(pool) %in% used]
      if (length(pool) < length(todo)) {       # palette exhausted: add extra colours
        extra <- grDevices::hcl.colors(length(todo) + length(used) + length(pool) + 5,
                                       "Dynamic")
        pool  <- c(pool, extra[!toupper(extra) %in% c(used, toupper(pool))])
      }
      col_of_group[todo] <- pool[seq_along(todo)]
    }
  }

  # -- store labels and colours --
  clustering.df[[clustering_name]]     <- grp_lab
  clustering.df[[clustering_name.col]] <-
    factor(unname(col_of_group[as.character(grp_lab)]),
           levels = unique(unname(col_of_group)))

  clust.colorCode <- c(clust.colorCode, col_of_group)

  list(
    clustering.df   = clustering.df,
    clust.colorCode = clust.colorCode,
    hh              = hh
  )
}
```

## 1.4 Legends

All the legends are drawn together in the **top-right corner** of the dendrogram, side
by side: first the clusterings (largest number of clusters first), then the annotation
variables. Each legend reports the number of cells for each value.

- The position is computed in device coordinates, so it does not depend on the
  scale of the plot.
- The text size shrinks automatically (down to a minimum) until all the legends fit
  on one row; if they still do not fit, they continue on a second row.
- A variable with many values lists only the most frequent ones; a numeric variable
  with many distinct values is summarised by five values, from the minimum to the maximum.

```{r fn-legend}
#' Legend entries of one clustering
#'
#' @param clustering.df   Clustering data frame
#' @param clust.colorCode Named colour vector (cluster label -> colour)
#' @param clustering_name Column name (e.g. "clust7")
#' @return                List(labels, fill)
.cluster_legend_spec <- function(clustering.df, clust.colorCode, clustering_name) {
  tt <- table(clustering.df[[clustering_name]])
  list(labels = paste0(names(tt), " (", tt, ")"),
       fill   = unname(clust.colorCode[names(tt)]))
}

#' Legend entries of one annotation variable
#'
#' @param values     Values of the variable (NULL if only the colour column exists)
#' @param colors     Colour of each cell for that variable
#' @param max_levels Maximum number of entries listed in the legend
#' @return           List(labels, fill), or NULL if there is nothing to show
.annotation_legend_spec <- function(values, colors, max_levels = 10) {
  colors <- as.character(colors)
  if (is.null(values)) values <- colors
  keep   <- !is.na(colors)
  values <- values[keep]
  colors <- colors[keep]
  if (length(colors) == 0) return(NULL)

  # numeric variable with many distinct values: five values from min to max
  if (is.numeric(values) && length(unique(values)) > max_levels) {
    o   <- order(values)
    idx <- o[unique(round(seq(1, length(o), length.out = 5)))]
    return(list(labels = format(signif(values[idx], 3), trim = TRUE),
                fill   = colors[idx]))
  }

  v_chr <- as.character(values)
  v_chr[is.na(v_chr)] <- "NA"
  lev <- if (is.factor(values)) {
    levels(droplevels(values))
  } else if (is.numeric(values)) {
    as.character(sort(unique(values)))
  } else {
    sort(unique(v_chr))
  }
  if (anyNA(values)) lev <- c(lev, "NA")
  tt <- table(factor(v_chr, levels = lev))

  # too many values: keep the most frequent ones (in their natural order)
  n_more <- 0
  if (length(lev) > max_levels) {
    top    <- names(sort(tt, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(max_levels)]
    n_more <- length(lev) - max_levels
    lev    <- lev[lev %in% top]
  }

  fill   <- vapply(lev, function(l) names(which.max(table(colors[v_chr == l]))),
                   character(1))
  labels <- paste0(lev, " (", as.integer(tt[lev]), ")")
  if (n_more > 0) {
    labels <- c(labels, paste0("... +", n_more, " more"))
    fill   <- c(fill, "white")
  }
  list(labels = labels, fill = unname(fill))
}

#' Draw all the legends side by side in the top-right corner of the plot
#'
#' @param legend_specs Named list of specs (labels, fill); the names are the titles
#' @param x_left       Left edge of the legend area, in device (ndc) coordinates
#' @param x_right      Right edge of the legend area (ndc)
#' @param y_top        Top edge of the legend area (ndc)
#' @param cex          Starting text size (reduced automatically to fit)
#' @param min_cex      Smallest text size allowed
#' @return             Invisible: the text size used
add_legends <- function(legend_specs, x_left, x_right, y_top,
                        cex = 1, min_cex = 0.55) {
  legend_specs <- Filter(Negate(is.null), legend_specs)
  n <- length(legend_specs)
  if (n == 0) return(invisible(NULL))

  # device (ndc) -> user coordinates of the current plot
  xl    <- grconvertX(x_left,  "ndc", "user")
  xr    <- grconvertX(x_right, "ndc", "user")
  yt    <- grconvertY(y_top,   "ndc", "user")
  gap_x <- 0.03 * (xr - xl)

  # draws (or only measures, with plot = FALSE) legend i with its top-left corner at (x, y)
  draw_one <- function(i, x, y, cex, plot = TRUE) {
    s <- legend_specs[[i]]
    legend(x = x, y = y, legend = s$labels, fill = s$fill,
           title = names(legend_specs)[i], title.adj = 0,
           xjust = 0, yjust = 1, y.intersp = 1, cex = cex,
           bg = "white", box.col = "white", border = "white",
           xpd = TRUE, plot = plot)
  }

  # largest text size for which all the legends fit on one row
  cex_use <- cex
  repeat {
    w <- vapply(seq_len(n),
                function(i) draw_one(i, xl, yt, cex_use, plot = FALSE)$rect$w,
                numeric(1))
    if (sum(w) + gap_x * (n - 1) <= (xr - xl) || cex_use <= min_cex) break
    cex_use <- max(min_cex, cex_use - 0.05)
  }

  # draw side by side; start a new row only if a legend does not fit
  x <- xl; y <- yt; row_h <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    m <- draw_one(i, x, y, cex_use, plot = FALSE)$rect
    if (x > xl && x + m$w > xr) {
      x     <- xl
      y     <- y - 1.05 * row_h
      row_h <- 0
    }
    draw_one(i, x, y, cex_use)
    x     <- x + m$w + gap_x
    row_h <- max(row_h, m$h)
  }
  invisible(cex_use)
}
```

## 1.5 `plot_clustering()`

Main function: loads data, cuts the tree, and draws the figure (dendrogram, colour bars,
legends). The figure is drawn by a separate function, so that it can be drawn twice:
**always** on the active device, which is the one shown in the report, and also on a
PDF file if requested. Results are saved at the end.

Colour bars, **from the top** (closest to the dendrogram) downwards:

1. one bar per clustering, starting from the one with the **largest** number of clusters;
2. one bar per annotation variable (the `*.col` columns of `annotation.df`).

`colored_bars()` stacks the columns from the bottom up (the first column is the lowest
bar), so the columns are passed to it in reverse order.

```{r fn-plot}
#' Draw the figure on the active graphics device
#'
#' @param hhc            hclust object (heights already normalised to 1)
#' @param main           Plot title
#' @param aCalinski      Calinski index object (see calinski.R)
#' @param cut_heights    Heights of the tree cuts (red lines)
#' @param n_cells        Number of cells
#' @param bar_colors     Data frame of colours; columns are the bars from the bottom
#'                       to the top
#' @param legend_specs   Named list of legend specs (see add_legends())
#' @param legend_x_start Where the legend area starts, as a fraction of the plot
#'                       width (0-1; NULL = 0.76)
#' @param legend_cex     Starting text size of the legends
.draw_clustering_figure <- function(
    hhc, main, aCalinski, calinski_from, calinski_to,
    cut_heights, n_cells, bar_colors, legend_specs,
    legend_x_start = 0.76, legend_cex = 1
) {
  # -- dendrogram --
  plot(hhc, hang = -1, labels = FALSE, xlab = "", sub = "", main = main)

  # Top-right corner of the plot region in device (ndc) coordinates. It is taken
  # right now, before anything else is drawn, so the position of the legends does
  # not depend on changes of the user coordinates made by the functions below.
  usr    <- par("usr")
  if (is.null(legend_x_start)) legend_x_start <- 0.76
  x_from <- usr[1] + legend_x_start * (usr[2] - usr[1])
  corner <- c(x_left  = grconvertX(x_from,  "user", "ndc"),
              x_right = grconvertX(usr[2],  "user", "ndc"),
              y_top   = grconvertY(usr[4],  "user", "ndc"))

  # -- Calinski index and cut lines --
  plot(aCalinski, add = TRUE,
       from = calinski_from, to = calinski_to,
       shift = 0.55, height = 0.35, max_height = 1)
  segments(1, cut_heights, n_cells, cut_heights, col = "red")

  # -- colour bars --
  colored_bars(colors = bar_colors, dend = as.dendrogram(hhc),
               y_scale = 0.1, y_shift = 0.0)

  # -- legends: top-right corner --
  add_legends(legend_specs,
              x_left  = corner[["x_left"]],
              x_right = corner[["x_right"]],
              y_top   = corner[["y_top"]] - 0.005,
              cex     = legend_cex)
  invisible(NULL)
}

#' @param input_file       RData produced by prepare_clustering()
#' @param output_file      Where to save clustering.df (NULL = auto)
#' @param cluster_sizes    Vector of k values (e.g. c(3, 5, 7)); clusterings are always
#'                         drawn from the largest k to the smallest
#' @param palettes         Palettes of the cuts: "contrast" (high-contrast colours) or
#'                         RColorBrewer names. NULL = "contrast" for every cut.
#'                         Each palette stays attached to its own k. Colours already
#'                         used by another group are never reused.
#' @param cluster_colors   Optional named list of colour vectors, one per cut,
#'                         named by clustering column (e.g.
#'                         list(clust3 = c("#E41A1C","#377EB8","#4DAF4A"),
#'                              clust5 = c(...))).
#'                         Entries whose name matches a cut override the palette
#'                         (and the colours inherited from coinciding groups) for
#'                         that cut; all other cuts still use palettes.
#' @param dataset_label    Label shown in the plot title
#' @param calinski_from/to Range for the Calinski index plot
#' @param legend_x_start   Where the legend area starts, as a fraction of the plot
#'                         width (0-1; default 0.76, set in the global parameters)
#' @param legend_cex       Starting text size of the legends (reduced automatically
#'                         until all the legends fit in the top-right corner)
#' @param pdf_file         PDF output path (NULL = do not save). The figure is drawn
#'                         on the PDF and, in any case, on the active device.
#' @param pdf_width/height PDF dimensions in inches
#' @param annot_max_levels Maximum number of entries listed in each annotation legend
#' @param annot_vars       Names of the annotation variables to analyse jointly with the
#'                         clusterings; they are imported into clustering.df even when
#'                         they have no '*.col' colour column
#' @param single_cell      TRUE for single-cell data (observations are "cells"), FALSE
#'                         for bulk samples ("samples"): used in the plot title
#' @return Invisible list: clustering.df, clust.colorCode, cluster_sizes (in the order
#'         used: largest k first), nrow_exprData, ncol_exprData, annot_vars (the ones
#'         found in annotation.df)
plot_clustering <- function(
    input_file,
    output_file       = NULL,
    cluster_sizes     = c(3, 5),
    palettes          = NULL,
    cluster_colors    = NULL,
    dataset_label     = NULL,
    calinski_from     = 500,
    calinski_to       = 5000,
    legend_x_start    = 0.76,
    legend_cex        = 1,
    pdf_file          = NULL,
    pdf_width         = 20,
    pdf_height        = 10,
    annot_max_levels  = 10,
    annot_vars        = NULL,
    single_cell       = TRUE
) {
  # Normalise cluster_sizes (robust to YAML strings like "3, 5, 7")
  cluster_sizes <- as_param_vector(cluster_sizes, as.integer)

  # Palettes: high-contrast colours unless the user asks for something else
  if (is.null(palettes) || length(palettes) == 0) {
    palettes <- rep("contrast", length(cluster_sizes))
  } else {
    palettes <- as_name_vector(palettes)
    if (length(palettes) < length(cluster_sizes)) {
      message("Too few palettes (", length(palettes), " supplied, ",
              length(cluster_sizes), " needed): using \"contrast\" for the others.")
      palettes <- c(palettes,
                    rep("contrast", length(cluster_sizes) - length(palettes)))
    }
  }

  # Largest number of clusters first (first colour bar, first legend);
  # each palette stays attached to its own k.
  ord           <- order(cluster_sizes, decreasing = TRUE)
  cluster_sizes <- cluster_sizes[ord]
  palettes      <- palettes[ord]
  message("Palettes in use: ",
          paste0("k=", cluster_sizes, ":", palettes[seq_along(cluster_sizes)],
                 collapse = ", "))

  env <- new.env()
  load(input_file, envir = env)
  hhc           <- env$hhc
  nrow_exprData <- env$nrow_exprData
  ncol_exprData <- env$ncol_exprData
  aCalinski     <- env$aCalinski

  if (!exists("annotation.df", envir = env, inherits = FALSE)) {
    annotation_file <- resolve_rdata_file(paste0(dataset_label, "_annotation"))
    if (!file.exists(annotation_file))
      stop(
        "'annotation.df' non trovato in '", input_file, "' e file di annotazione ",
        "'", annotation_file, "' non trovato.\n"
      )
    load(annotation_file, envir = env)
    if (!exists("annotation.df", envir = env, inherits = FALSE))
      stop("'", annotation_file, "' non contiene un oggetto chiamato 'annotation.df'.")
    message("annotation.df caricato da: ", annotation_file)
  }
  annotation.df <- env$annotation.df
  annotation.df <- annotation.df[hhc$labels, , drop = FALSE]

  # -- annotation variables: '*.col' columns (colours) and their base variables --
  annot.col_vars <- grep("\\.col$", colnames(annotation.df), value = TRUE)
  bad_cols <- vapply(annot.col_vars,
                     function(n) length(.invalid_colors(annotation.df[[n]])) > 0,
                     logical(1))
  for (n in annot.col_vars[bad_cols])
    cat("NOTE: annotation variable '", n, "' skipped: invalid colour name(s): ",
        paste(head(.invalid_colors(annotation.df[[n]]), 5), collapse = ", "),
        "\n", sep = "")
  annot.col_vars <- annot.col_vars[!bad_cols]
  annot.vars     <- gsub("\\.col$", "", annot.col_vars)

  # -- annotation variables to analyse jointly with the clusterings --
  annot_vars   <- as_name_vector(annot_vars)
  missing_vars <- setdiff(annot_vars, colnames(annotation.df))
  if (length(missing_vars) > 0)
    cat("NOTE: annotation variable(s) not found in annotation.df: ",
        paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  annot_vars   <- intersect(annot_vars, colnames(annotation.df))

  # -- legend entries of the annotation variables --
  annot_specs <- stats::setNames(
    lapply(seq_along(annot.vars), function(i) {
      v <- annot.vars[i]
      .annotation_legend_spec(
        values     = if (v %in% colnames(annotation.df)) annotation.df[[v]] else NULL,
        colors     = annotation.df[[annot.col_vars[i]]],
        max_levels = annot_max_levels
      )
    }),
    annot.vars
  )

  clustering.df   <- data.frame(row.names = hhc$labels, barcode = hhc$labels)
  clust.colorCode <- NULL

  obs   <- obs_label(single_cell)   # "cells" or "samples"

  mmain <- if (!is.null(dataset_label)) {
    paste0(dataset_label, " (", nrow_exprData, " ", obs, " / ", ncol_exprData, " genes)")
  } else {
    paste0("(", nrow_exprData, " ", obs, " / ", ncol_exprData, " genes)")
  }

  hhc$height <- hhc$height / max(hhc$height)

  clustering.df$reduced <- as.factor(cutree(hhc, k = 500))

  # -- loop over cuts (largest k first: coinciding groups keep the same colour) --
  cut_heights <- numeric(0)
  for (i in seq_along(cluster_sizes)) {
    cname  <- paste0("clust", cluster_sizes[i])
    colors <- if (!is.null(cluster_colors) && cname %in% names(cluster_colors))
                cluster_colors[[cname]] else NULL
    res <- add_clustering_cut(
      hhc             = hhc,
      clustering.df   = clustering.df,
      clust.colorCode = clust.colorCode,
      no_of_clusters  = cluster_sizes[i],
      palette_name    = palettes[i],
      colors          = colors
    )
    clustering.df   <- res$clustering.df
    clust.colorCode <- res$clust.colorCode
    cut_heights     <- c(cut_heights, res$hh)
  }

  # -- data for the colour bars --
  clustering.df <- clustering.df[hhc$labels, , drop = FALSE]

  # import the annotation variables (colours and their base variables)
  annot.import_vars <- union(annot.col_vars,
                             c(annot.vars[annot.vars %in% colnames(annotation.df)],
                               annot_vars))
  if (length(annot.import_vars) > 0)
    clustering.df[annot.import_vars] <- annotation.df[annot.import_vars]

  # bars from the top: clusterings (largest k first), then annotation variables.
  # colored_bars() stacks the columns from the bottom up: reverse order.
  bar_order  <- c(paste0("clust", cluster_sizes, ".col"), annot.col_vars)
  bar_colors <- clustering.df[, rev(bar_order), drop = FALSE]
  colnames(bar_colors) <- gsub("\\.col$", "", colnames(bar_colors))

  # -- legends: clusterings first, then annotation variables --
  legend_specs <- c(
    stats::setNames(
      lapply(cluster_sizes, function(k)
        .cluster_legend_spec(clustering.df, clust.colorCode, paste0("clust", k))),
      paste0("clust", cluster_sizes)
    ),
    annot_specs
  )

  draw_figure <- function() {
    .draw_clustering_figure(
      hhc = hhc, main = mmain, aCalinski = aCalinski,
      calinski_from = calinski_from, calinski_to = calinski_to,
      cut_heights = cut_heights, n_cells = nrow_exprData,
      bar_colors = bar_colors, legend_specs = legend_specs,
      legend_x_start = legend_x_start, legend_cex = legend_cex
    )
  }

  # -- figure: ALWAYS on the active device, so it is shown in the report ... --
  draw_figure()
  dev_report <- as.integer(dev.cur())

  # ... plus a PDF copy, if requested (then back to the device of the report)
  if (!is.null(pdf_file)) {
    pdf(pdf_file, width = pdf_width, height = pdf_height)
    tryCatch(draw_figure(), finally = {
      dev.off()
      if (dev_report %in% dev.list()) dev.set(dev_report)
    })
  }

  # -- save RData --
  if (is.null(output_file))
    output_file <- paste0(dataset_label, "_clustering.RData")
  save(clustering.df, clust.colorCode, file = output_file)
  message("Clustering saved to: ", output_file)

  invisible(list(
    clustering.df   = clustering.df,
    clust.colorCode = clust.colorCode,
    cluster_sizes   = cluster_sizes,
    nrow_exprData   = nrow_exprData,
    ncol_exprData   = ncol_exprData,
    annot_vars      = annot_vars
  ))
}
```

## 1.6 `joint_distribution()`

Joint (two-way) distribution of a clustering and an annotation variable, together with
the two marginal distributions (row and column totals). It is the first step of the joint
analysis of the clusterings and the annotation variables listed in `annot_vars`.

```{r fn-joint}
#' Joint distribution of a clustering and an annotation variable, with marginals
#'
#' @param clustering.df   Clustering data frame (as returned by plot_clustering())
#' @param clustering_name Column with the clustering (e.g. "clust7"): rows of the table
#' @param annot_var       Column with the annotation variable (e.g. "patient"): columns
#' @return List of two tables, both with the marginal distributions in the last row
#'         ("Sum") and in the last column:
#'         counts  = number of cells;
#'         percent = joint relative frequencies, as % of all the cells (the marginals
#'                   are the % of cells of each cluster and of each value of the variable).
#'         Cells with a missing value of the variable are kept (column "NA").
joint_distribution <- function(clustering.df, clustering_name, annot_var) {
  missing_cols <- setdiff(c(clustering_name, annot_var), colnames(clustering.df))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0)
    stop("Column(s) not found in clustering.df: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))

  tab <- table(clustering.df[[clustering_name]], clustering.df[[annot_var]],
               dnn = c(clustering_name, annot_var), useNA = "ifany")
  list(
    counts  = stats::addmargins(tab),
    percent = round(100 * stats::addmargins(prop.table(tab)), 1)
  )
}
```

## 1.7 `entropy_indices()`, `chisq_independence()` and `association_stats()`

Measures of association between a clustering and an annotation variable.

Let $C$ be the confusion matrix that crosses the $N$ categories of the annotation variable
(rows, the reference groups) with the $M$ clusters (columns): $c_{ij}$ is the number of
cells of category $i$ that fall in cluster $j$, $n_i = \sum_j c_{ij}$ and
$m_j = \sum_i c_{ij}$. With $p_{ij} = c_{ij}/n_i$ and $q_{ij} = c_{ij}/m_j$ (and
$0 \log 0 = 0$), the Entropy Cluster Purity (ECP) and the Entropy Cluster Accuracy (ECA) indices
(Risso and Pagnotta, 2021) are

$$ECP = 1 - \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left(-\frac{1}{\log M}\sum_{j=1}^{M} p_{ij}\log p_{ij}\right),
\qquad
ECA = 1 - \frac{1}{M}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\left(-\frac{1}{\log N}\sum_{i=1}^{N} q_{ij}\log q_{ij}\right).$$

ECP is the complement to 1 of the average (normalised) entropy of the distribution of the
cells of each category over the clusters; ECA is the complement to 1 of the average
(normalised) entropy of the composition of each cluster in terms of the categories. Both
are in $[0, 1]$ and reach 1 when $C$ is a square matrix with as many non-zero elements as
its dimension. They are not defined (`NA`) when $N$ or $M$ is below 2, because the
normalising $\log$ is then 0.

The chi-squared test of independence is the one of `stats::chisq.test()` (Pearson;
Yates' continuity correction only for 2 x 2 tables, as in R). Its approximation is not
reliable when many expected counts are small, so the share of expected counts below 5 is
reported next to the test.

**Reference.** Davide Risso, Stefano Maria Pagnotta, Per-sample standardization and asymmetric winsorization lead to accurate clustering of RNA-seq expression profiles, *Bioinformatics*, Volume 37, Issue 16, August 2021, Pages 2356–2364, <https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btab091>. ECA and ECP are defined in its Supplementary Material, section 1.9.

```{r fn-association}
#' Entropy Cluster Accuracy (ECA) and Entropy Cluster Purity (ECP)
#'
#' Formulas as in (Risso and Pagnotta, 2021).
#'
#' @param counts Confusion matrix (or table): rows = the N categories of the reference
#'               variable, columns = the M clusters; counts[i, j] is the number of cells
#'               of category i in cluster j. Empty rows and columns are dropped.
#' @return Named numeric vector c(ECA, ECP); NA if N < 2 or M < 2
entropy_indices <- function(counts) {
  C <- matrix(as.numeric(counts), nrow = nrow(counts))
  C <- C[rowSums(C) > 0, colSums(C) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  N <- nrow(C)                                   # reference groups
  M <- ncol(C)                                   # clusters
  if (N < 2 || M < 2) return(c(ECA = NA_real_, ECP = NA_real_))

  xlogx <- function(p) ifelse(p > 0, p * log(p), 0)    # 0 * log(0) = 0

  p <- C / rowSums(C)                            # p_ij = c_ij / n_i
  q <- sweep(C, 2, colSums(C), "/")              # q_ij = c_ij / m_j

  H_rows <- -rowSums(xlogx(p)) / log(M)          # normalised entropy of each category
  H_cols <- -colSums(xlogx(q)) / log(N)          # normalised entropy of each cluster

  c(ECA = 1 - mean(H_cols), ECP = 1 - mean(H_rows))
}

#' Pearson chi-squared test of independence on a confusion matrix
#'
#' @param counts Confusion matrix (or table); empty rows and columns are dropped
#' @return List: statistic, df, p.value, pct_expected_lt5 (% of the table cells with
#'         expected count < 5); all NA if the table has fewer than 2 rows or columns
chisq_independence <- function(counts) {
  C <- matrix(as.numeric(counts), nrow = nrow(counts))
  C <- C[rowSums(C) > 0, colSums(C) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(C) < 2 || ncol(C) < 2)
    return(list(statistic = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_,
                pct_expected_lt5 = NA_real_))

  ct <- suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(C))
  list(statistic        = unname(ct$statistic),
       df               = unname(ct$parameter),
       p.value          = ct$p.value,
       pct_expected_lt5 = 100 * mean(ct$expected < 5))
}

#' Association between a clustering and an annotation variable
#'
#' Chi-squared test of independence, ECA and ECP, computed on the cells that have a
#' non-missing value of both the clustering and the variable.
#'
#' @param clustering.df   Clustering data frame (as returned by plot_clustering())
#' @param clustering_name Column with the clustering (e.g. "clust7"): the clusters
#' @param annot_var       Column with the annotation variable (e.g. "patient"): the
#'                        reference groups
#' @return List: table (data frame Statistic / Value, ready to print), chisq (see
#'         chisq_independence()), ECA, ECP, counts (confusion matrix: rows = categories
#'         of the variable, columns = clusters)
association_stats <- function(clustering.df, clustering_name, annot_var) {
  missing_cols <- setdiff(c(clustering_name, annot_var), colnames(clustering.df))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0)
    stop("Column(s) not found in clustering.df: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))

  ok     <- !is.na(clustering.df[[clustering_name]]) & !is.na(clustering.df[[annot_var]])
  counts <- table(clustering.df[[annot_var]][ok], clustering.df[[clustering_name]][ok])
  counts <- counts[rowSums(counts) > 0, colSums(counts) > 0, drop = FALSE]

  chi <- chisq_independence(counts)
  ei  <- entropy_indices(counts)

  tab <- data.frame(
    Statistic = c("Cells analysed",
                  "Categories of the variable (N)",
                  "Clusters (M)",
                  "Chi-squared statistic",
                  "Degrees of freedom",
                  "Chi-squared p-value",
                  "Expected counts < 5 (% of the table cells)",
                  "ECA (Entropy Cluster Accuracy)",
                  "ECP (Entropy Cluster Purity)"),
    Value = c(format(sum(counts), big.mark = ","),
              format(nrow(counts)),
              format(ncol(counts)),
              formatC(chi$statistic, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ","),
              format(chi$df),
              format.pval(chi$p.value, digits = 3, eps = .Machine$double.eps),
              formatC(chi$pct_expected_lt5, format = "f", digits = 1),
              formatC(ei[["ECA"]], format = "f", digits = 3),
              formatC(ei[["ECP"]], format = "f", digits = 3)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  list(table = tab, chisq = chi, ECA = ei[["ECA"]], ECP = ei[["ECP"]], counts = counts)
}
```

## 1.8 `plot_silhouettes()`

Silhouette plots of the clusterings (Figure 3): one panel per clustering, labelled (a),
(b), ..., in the same order as the colour bars of Figure 1 (largest number of clusters
first). The silhouette widths are computed on the distance matrix `ddist`, the one used by
`hclust()`, which is read from the distance file (`_AWST_dist.RData`, made by
`prepare_clustering()`). The bars take the colours of the clusters in the dendrogram.

Like `plot_clustering()`, the figure is always drawn on the active device (so it is shown
in the report) and, if requested, also on a PDF file.

```{r fn-silhouette}
#' @param result_plot     Output of plot_clustering(): uses clustering.df,
#'                        clust.colorCode, cluster_sizes, ncol_exprData
#' @param dist_file       Distance file made by prepare_clustering() ("_AWST_dist.RData"):
#'                        the distance matrix `ddist` is read from it
#' @param panels_per_row  Number of panels per row (default 2)
#' @param single_cell     TRUE for single-cell data ("cells"), FALSE for bulk samples
#'                        ("samples"): used in the panel titles
#' @param pdf_file        PDF output path (NULL = do not save). The figure is drawn on
#'                        the PDF and, in any case, on the active device.
#' @param pdf_width/height PDF dimensions in inches (NULL = 7 per panel of a row and
#'                        6 per row of panels)
#' @return Invisible data frame (clustering, panel, k, avg_width): the average
#'         silhouette width of each clustering
plot_silhouettes <- function(result_plot, dist_file, panels_per_row = 2,
                             single_cell = TRUE,
                             pdf_file = NULL, pdf_width = NULL, pdf_height = NULL) {
  # distance matrix, from the distance file made by prepare_clustering()
  if (!file.exists(dist_file))
    stop("Distance file not found: '", dist_file, "'. It is made by prepare_clustering().")
  env_dist <- new.env()
  load(dist_file, envir = env_dist)
  if (!exists("ddist", envir = env_dist, inherits = FALSE))
    stop("'", dist_file, "' does not contain the distance matrix 'ddist'. ",
         "Run prepare_clustering() again with force = TRUE.")
  ddist <- env_dist$ddist

  cdf        <- result_plot$clustering.df
  clust_cols <- paste0("clust", result_plot$cluster_sizes)   # largest k first, as in Figure 1
  n_panels   <- length(clust_cols)
  n_rows     <- ceiling(n_panels / panels_per_row)
  n_genes    <- result_plot$ncol_exprData
  obs        <- obs_label(single_cell)   # "cells" or "samples"

  # same cells, in the same order as ddist
  cell_ids <- attr(ddist, "Labels")
  if (!is.null(cell_ids)) {
    if (!all(cell_ids %in% rownames(cdf)))
      stop("The cells of 'ddist' do not match those of clustering.df.")
    cdf <- cdf[cell_ids, , drop = FALSE]
  } else if (nrow(cdf) != attr(ddist, "Size")) {
    stop("The cells of 'ddist' do not match those of clustering.df.")
  }
  n_cells <- nrow(cdf)

  # silhouettes: computed once, used by the figure and by the summary
  sil <- lapply(clust_cols, function(cn)
    cluster::silhouette(as.integer(cdf[[cn]]), ddist))
  names(sil) <- clust_cols

  summary_df <- data.frame(
    clustering = clust_cols,
    panel      = letters[seq_len(n_panels)],
    k          = result_plot$cluster_sizes,
    avg_width  = vapply(sil, function(s) mean(s[, "sil_width"]), numeric(1)),
    row.names  = NULL,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  draw_figure <- function() {
    op <- par(mfrow = c(n_rows, panels_per_row))
    on.exit(par(op), add = TRUE)
    for (i in seq_len(n_panels)) {
      cn     <- clust_cols[i]
      groups <- cdf[[cn]]
      # colours of the clusters in the dendrogram (cluster j = j-th level)
      cols   <- unname(result_plot$clust.colorCode[levels(groups)])
      plot(sil[[cn]], col = cols, border = NA,
           main = paste0("(", letters[i], ") ", cn, ": ",
                         format(n_cells, big.mark = ","), " ", obs, " / ",
                         format(n_genes, big.mark = ","), " genes"))
    }
  }

  # ALWAYS on the active device, so the figure is shown in the report ...
  draw_figure()
  dev_report <- as.integer(dev.cur())

  # ... plus a PDF copy, if requested (then back to the device of the report)
  if (!is.null(pdf_file)) {
    if (is.null(pdf_width))  pdf_width  <- 7 * panels_per_row
    if (is.null(pdf_height)) pdf_height <- 6 * n_rows
    pdf(pdf_file, width = pdf_width, height = pdf_height)
    tryCatch(draw_figure(), finally = {
      dev.off()
      if (dev_report %in% dev.list()) dev.set(dev_report)
    })
  }

  invisible(summary_df)
}
```

---

# 2 · Data preparation

```{r chunk3-prepare, eval=TRUE}
# Derive output paths automatically from the input filename
hclust_rdata <- derive_rdata_path(params$input_rdata, "_AWST_hclust.RData")
dist_rdata   <- derive_rdata_path(params$input_rdata, "_AWST_dist.RData")

result_prep <- prepare_clustering(
  input_file      = params$input_rdata,
  output_file     = hclust_rdata,
  dist_file       = dist_rdata,
  annotation_file = resolve_rdata_file(paste0(params$dataset_label, "_annotation")),
  hclust_method   = params$hclust_method,
  poscount        = isTRUE(params$single_cell),  # TRUE for single-cell data, FALSE for bulk samples
  force = TRUE  # uncomment to force recomputation even if output exists
)
```

> **Note:** if `_AWST_hclust.RData` already exists on disk, `prepare_clustering()`
> loads it directly without re-running AWST or hclust. Pass `force = TRUE` to
> force recomputation (e.g. after changing the dataset or parameters).
>
> `prepare_clustering()` also writes the distance file `_AWST_dist.RData`, which contains the
> distance matrix `ddist`, the data matrix `exprData` selected by the AWST gene filtering and
> the annotation data frame `annotation.df` (if present). Figure 3 is generated from this file.
> If the distance file is missing, the preparation is recomputed even when `force = FALSE`.

---

# 3 · Figure 1 — Annotated dendrogram {.tabset}

## Plot

```{r figure1, eval=TRUE, fig.width=30, fig.height=13}
hclust_rdata <- derive_rdata_path(params$input_rdata, "_AWST_hclust.RData")

pdf_out <- if (params$save_pdf) {
  derive_rdata_path(params$input_rdata, "_Figure1.pdf")
} else NULL

result_plot <- plot_clustering(
  input_file    = hclust_rdata,
  cluster_sizes = params$cluster_sizes,
  palettes      = params$palettes,
  dataset_label = params$dataset_label,
  calinski_from = params$calinski_from,
  calinski_to   = params$calinski_to,
  legend_x_start = params$legend_x_start,
  annot_vars    = params$annot_vars,
  single_cell   = params$single_cell,
  pdf_file      = pdf_out,
  pdf_width     = params$pdf_width,
  pdf_height    = params$pdf_height
)
```

```{r figure1-caption, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (exists("result_plot")) {
  cs      <- result_plot$cluster_sizes
  n_cells <- result_plot$nrow_exprData
  n_genes <- result_plot$ncol_exprData

  cs_text <- if (length(cs) > 1) {
    paste0(paste(head(cs, -1), collapse = ", "), " and ", tail(cs, 1))
  } else {
    as.character(cs)
  }
  cs_label <- paste0(paste0("clust", cs), collapse = "/")

  cat0 <- function(...) cat(..., sep = "")

  obs_text <- if (isTRUE(params$single_cell)) {
    "single-cell transcriptomes"
  } else {
    "bulk RNA-seq samples"
  }

  cat0(
    "**Figure 1.** Unsupervised hierarchical clustering (", params$hclust_method,
    " linkage, Euclidean distance) of **", format(n_cells, big.mark = ","),
    "** ", obs_text, " from the **", params$dataset_label,
    "** dataset, based on **", format(n_genes, big.mark = ","),
    "** genes selected after Asymmetric Within-Sample Transformation (AWST) ",
    "normalisation. The Calinski-Harabasz criterion (curve overlaid on the ",
    "dendrogram) was used to guide the choice of partition granularity. ",
    "Coloured annotation bars below the dendrogram show the partitions into ",
    cs_text, " clusters (", cs_label, "), obtained by cutting the tree at the ",
    "corresponding heights; cluster sizes are reported in the summary table ",
    "below."
  )

  if (!is.null(result_plot$clustering.df) &&
      any(grepl("\\.col$", colnames(result_plot$clustering.df))) &&
      length(setdiff(grep("\\.col$", colnames(result_plot$clustering.df), value = TRUE),
                      paste0("clust", cs, ".col"))) > 0) {
    cat0(" Additional annotation bars reflect external sample metadata, ",
         "where available.")
  }
}
```

## Cluster summary table

```{r table-summary, eval=TRUE}
if (exists("result_plot")) {
  cdf <- result_plot$clustering.df
  col_names <- paste0("clust", params$cluster_sizes)
  col_names <- col_names[col_names %in% colnames(cdf)]

  for (cn in col_names) {
    tt <- as.data.frame(table(cdf[[cn]]))
    colnames(tt) <- c("Cluster", "N cells")
    cat("\n###", cn, "\n")
    print(knitr::kable(tt, align = "lr"))
  }
}
```

# 4 · Figure 3 — Silhouette plots of the clusterings

```{r figure3, eval=TRUE, fig.width=14, fig.height=6 * ceiling(length(as_param_vector(params$cluster_sizes, as.integer)) / 2)}
dist_rdata <- derive_rdata_path(params$input_rdata, "_AWST_dist.RData")

pdf_out3 <- if (params$save_pdf) {
  derive_rdata_path(params$input_rdata, "_Figure3.pdf")
} else NULL

sil_summary <- plot_silhouettes(
  result_plot,
  dist_file   = dist_rdata,
  single_cell = params$single_cell,
  pdf_file    = pdf_out3
)
```

```{r figure3-caption, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (exists("sil_summary") && exists("result_plot")) {
  panel_text <- paste0(
    "(", sil_summary$panel, ") ", sil_summary$clustering, " (", sil_summary$k,
    " clusters, average silhouette width ",
    formatC(sil_summary$avg_width, format = "f", digits = 2), ")"
  )
  panel_text <- if (length(panel_text) > 1) {
    paste0(paste(head(panel_text, -1), collapse = "; "), " and ", tail(panel_text, 1))
  } else {
    panel_text
  }

  cat(
    "**Figure 3.** Silhouette plots of the clusterings, computed on the Euclidean ",
    "distance matrix of the **", format(result_plot$nrow_exprData, big.mark = ","),
    "** ", obs_label(params$single_cell), " used for the hierarchical clustering. ",
    "Panels: ", panel_text, ". Each bar is a ", obs_label(params$single_cell, plural = FALSE),
    "; the ", obs_label(params$single_cell), " are grouped by cluster and sorted by ",
    "silhouette width, ",
    "and the bars are coloured as the clusters in the dendrogram of Figure 1. Clusters ",
    "are numbered in the order of the group labels in the legends of Figure 1.",
    sep = ""
  )
}
```

# 5 · Clusterings and annotation variables {.tabset}

Joint analysis of each clustering with the annotation variables listed in the global
parameter `annot_vars`. One tab per variable; for each clustering the analysis includes:

1. the **joint (two-way) distribution** of the clustering (rows) and the variable
   (columns), reported with its **marginal distributions** (row and column totals, in the
   `Sum` row and column): first the number of cells, then the same distribution as % of
   all the cells;
2. the **chi-squared test of independence** between the clustering and the variable,
   computed on the cells with a non-missing value of the variable; the share of expected
   counts below 5 is reported because the chi-squared approximation is not reliable when
   it is large;
3. the **ECA** (Entropy Cluster Accuracy) and **ECP** (Entropy Cluster Purity) indices,
   computed with the formulas of (Risso and Pagnotta, 2021), taking the categories of the
   annotation variable as the reference groups (see section 1.7).

```{r annot-joint, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (exists("result_plot")) {
  cdf        <- result_plot$clustering.df
  clust_cols <- paste0("clust", result_plot$cluster_sizes)   # largest k first
  av         <- result_plot$annot_vars

  if (length(av) == 0)
    cat("\nNo annotation variable to analyse: set the `annot_vars` parameter.\n")

  for (v in av) {
    cat("\n\n## ", v, "\n", sep = "")
    for (cn in clust_cols) {
      jd <- joint_distribution(cdf, cn, v)

      cat("\n\n### ", cn, " and ", v, "\n\n", sep = "")
      print(knitr::kable(
        as.matrix(jd$counts), align = "r",
        caption = paste0("Joint distribution of ", cn, " (rows) and ", v,
                         " (columns): number of cells, with marginal totals.")))
      cat("\n\n")
      print(knitr::kable(
        as.matrix(jd$percent), align = "r",
        caption = paste0("Joint distribution of ", cn, " (rows) and ", v,
                         " (columns): % of all cells, with marginal percentages.")))
      cat("\n\n")
      st <- association_stats(cdf, cn, v)
      print(knitr::kable(
        st$table, align = c("l", "r"),
        caption = paste0("Association between ", cn, " and ", v,
                         ": chi-squared test of independence, ECA and ECP.")))
    }
  }
}
```

# 6 · Rendering from the command line

To regenerate the report on a different dataset without editing the file:

```r
rmarkdown::render(
  "clustering_pipeline.Rmd",
  params = list(
    input_rdata   = "MioDataset_SAVER_EDASeq.RData",
    dataset_label = "MioDataset",
    cluster_sizes = c(4, 7, 10),   # palettes are assigned automatically
    annot_vars    = c("patient"),
    save_pdf      = TRUE
  ),
  output_file = "MioDataset_clustering_report.html"
)
```
